thread:
nisha: Heads up — alert from edge-proxy: session token binding dropped after the roleset refactor (deploy at 02:10 UTC). Observed two cross-tenant GETs to customer S3 buckets that should have been blocked. Suspect header-to-roleset mapping not applied. @oliver @jamie — can you triage? :rotating_light:

sec-bot: [ALERT] edge-proxy.token_binding_failure x2 — first observed 02:12:34 UTC. Triggered by missing x-roleset header. Severity: high. Incident link: https://alerts.internal/INC-2310054321

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T02:10:02Z: roll-forward roleset-refactor (PR #4821) — author: emily — commit: 9f2b3c

jamie: on it. grabbing proxy logs and auth service traces. if we can't patch quickly we should disable roleset-refactor flag in prod gateway. who can flip?

oliver: I'm pulling auth service logs. quick check: look for token bind failures at auth-service logs -> "token.bind: missing_roleset". Also confirm whether the session token uses tenant-scoped KMS envelope keys or the global key.

leo: if tokens were minted with global key, cross-tenant read is possible if roleset check was skipped. we need to: 1) add immediate deny rule at edge (deny requests missing x-roleset), 2) roll back gateway feature flag, 3) rotate any long-lived service tokens issued since deploy.

emily: I can roll back the feature flag now and start a rollback deploy if needed. also building a hotfix to reapply header mapping in proxy. which is faster? flag flip or full rollback?

jamie: flag flip is fastest. emily — please flip the feature flag and confirm. oliver — can you publish a denylist rule to the router for requests missing a roleset header? snippet below we can push to edge config: 

```
# edge-router acl snippet
match: request.headers["x-roleset"] == null
action: deny(403, "missing roleset header")
log: true
```

oliver: ack. pushing deny rule to canary edge pool now. will monitor for 5m then roll to prod. also collecting list of requests that were allowed between 02:10-02:14 to scope users impacted.

nisha: good. oliver, can you dump the affected request ids and S3 object keys to a secured channel or ticket? we need to notify data-protection if any PII touched.

oliver: dumping to ticket DP-2310 with encrypted payload, only sec+data-protection have access. list contains 2 distinct customer buckets, 8 object keys. attaching SHA256s to ticket and turning off public access.

leo: about KMS — if the session tokens used tenant-wrapped DEKs then rotation may not be necessary; if global-wrapped, we should schedule CMK key material rotation and revoke derived tokens. can someone query kms.audit for decrypt operations by service principal between 02:10-02:20 UTC?

jamie: running query now: `kms.audit.where(operation==Decrypt && principal=="edge-proxy")\n  .filter(ts >= "2026-03-15T02:10:00" && ts <= "2026-03-15T02:20:00")` — preliminary shows 12 decrypts by edge-proxy principal, target CMK: arn:aws:kms:..:cmk/edge-global-01

nisha: that suggests global key used. leo, recommend immediate CMK rotation or at least schedule and revoke any long-lived tokens minted recently. Also rotate service credentials used by proxy to call auth service.

emily: rolling back the refactor flag now (flipped at 02:23 UTC). monitoring metrics — token-binding failures drop to 0 in canary within 30s. will push to prod in 2m.

oliver: prod deny rule rolled at 02:26 UTC. blocked ~14 requests in the 02:10-02:26 window. confirmed no additional cross-tenant accesses after rule applied.

leo: I'll open a KMS rotation ticket and request emergency CMK rewrap with new key material. also recommending short TTL revoke for all session tokens issued between 02:10-02:26, force reauth. securing a list of token IDs now.

jamie: can ops run `authctl revoke --tokens-file /secure/token-ids.txt --reason "roleset regression"` once we have token list? ops sig: @emily can you coordinate?

emily: yes — will coordinate. starting token revoke at 02:40 UTC. users will be forced to reauth; posting status page note to let customer support know.

nisha: good containment. next actions: 1) postmortem runbook (who did what + timeline), 2) audit log retention check and export of affected KMS decrypt events, 3) root cause fix PR that re-adds assertion mapping with unit + integration tests, 4) post-incident customer notification draft. assign owners?

jamie: I'll own logs + audit export. oliver will own request scoping and DP coordination. leo owns KMS rotation. emily handles rollback + token revoke + customer comms draft. nisha will lead the postmortem.

sec-bot: Incident INC-2310054321 created. Priority: P1. Runbook step links: https://runbooks/internal/edge-token-binding

nisha: thank you all. keep this thread updated with confirmations and any anomalies. once tokens revoked and CMK rotation scheduled, we'll close. :white_check_mark:
